table_reddening.source: mw_removed: unknown -- the paper corrects its own photometry, not this table's: "To correct for reddening, we consider both Galactic and intrinsic host extinction.  We estimate and correct for Galactic extinction using dustmaps from [137]." -- but the vendored CSV is a five-source compilation (`reference`: arXiv:2510.18854 x16, 2510.23732 x7, 2510.17104 x42, 2510.24620 x92, 2510.01142 x44 rows) with no per-row extinction flag, and only one of those five papers was read; declaring `true` or `false` for all 201 rows would be a guess about 194 rows no source ever stated, so the state stays `unknown`.  host_removed: unknown -- the paper measures host dust and then refuses to let it be used as a measurement: the Na I D relation "A_v^host = 0.78 (+/- 0.15) EW_NaID" applied to the LRIS spectrum of UT 2025-08-25 gives "E(B-V) ~ 0.29 mag and A_v^host ~ 0.89 mag ... (i.e. R_v = 3.1)", immediately qualified by "We caution that since low-resolution spectra are being used, this estimate is best used as an upper limit on the extinction" -- an upper limit is not an amount removed, and the compilation carries no removal flag either.

unfold.correction_model: per-epoch, penalised second difference in time
unfold.gain_definition: dM_band / d(log10 L_nu at the node), finite difference on the assembled surface; -2.5 is the delta-band limit

band_admission.rule: one departure at a time, worst excess first, undone when it pushed a band that was inside the cap outside it

template.label: AT 2025ulz / ZTF 25abjmnps (young stripped-envelope Type IIb supernova coincident with the sub-threshold trigger S250818k)
template.z_source: Kasliwal et al. 2025, arXiv:2510.23732v1 (read in full), spectroscopy: "In order to derive a redshift from the spectra, we use multiple host galaxy emission lines that yield z=0.0848 or 399.4 Mpc, which we adopt throughout." -- adopted verbatim; no error is quoted (so none is invented) and no reference frame is stated (so `frame` stays undeclared).  The same sentence carries the distance the paper pairs with that redshift; 399.4 Mpc corresponds to a distance modulus of 38.01, kept as a cross-check in docs/VALIDATION.md and never an input.

distance.source: z = 0.0848 sits above the 0.02 peculiar-velocity guard, so no `allow_low_z` flag is needed.  The paper's "399.4 Mpc" follows from that same redshift under a cosmology the sentence does not state -- it is not an independent distance indicator, so `kind: measured` would be fiction; it is kept only as the cross-check above.  The default cosmology is used and named in every result's provenance via `constants.DEFAULT_COSMOLOGY_NAME`.
